name: HISP- The Route of the Week
description:

The overall standings of the weekly league will be based on ZRS and will be available on ZwiftPower. https://zwiftpower.com/league.php?id=3242

Podrás repetir la carrera tantas veces como quieras, y veremos quién es el más rápido cada semana.
La clasificación general de la liga semanal se regirá por ZRS y estará disponible en ZwiftPower. https://zwiftpower.com/league.php?id=3242

name: 3R True2 Steady Ride [2.0w/kg avg]
description:
This is a 3R Group Ride Event. Your co-operation and teamwork is essential to the success of the ride and we ask that no riders ride off the front of the group. The event is designed as part of 3R’s package of #ProStyleTraining events to assist with the attainment of your training goals and may include intervals over and below the ride average parameters. This is not a race so please follow the leader beacon's (Yellow) instructions and if you are feeling strong, please help the keeper beacon (Red) to assist other riders back to the pack.  We welcome good banter and aim to create a fun, social atmosphere for your training. We welcome any feedback on our Facebook page https://www.facebook.com/groups/ClubWorldBicycleRelief/ #Team3R #Ride3R #RideRaceRaise.

#3r

name: SROZ's The Tour de Living Room
description:
Welcome to the ultimate test of human endurance, uncalibrated hardware, and aggressive air conditioning.

The Tour de Living Room takes you through the high-stakes, zero-draft corridors of your spare bedroom. Expect relentless pace, questionable weight metrics, and zero cornering brake checks.

This 42 km prologue features 309 meters of punchy elevation gain over varied terrain, offering a fast-paced environment where dynamic pack riding and well-timed power-ups will determine the winner. Be ready for a rapid start right out of the pens, as the field quickly settles into a high-tempo rhythm across the flats before tackling the key gradient shifts.

To ensure fair and competitive racing for all participants, please calibrate your smart trainer or power meter prior to joining the event pen. Racers are encouraged to keep their profile height and weight accurate to maintain realistic pack dynamics and power-to-weight metrics (W/kg). Heart rate monitors are strongly recommended for category placement and post-race verification.

Dust off your fans, top off your bottles, and get ready for an exciting kickoff to our upcoming series!

name: Workout Wednesday Run
description:
Join the Zwift Runners for a group run workout that will be of benefit to all distance runners.

The speeds for each group are based on a threshold speed of A group 15 kph, B 13 kph, C 11 kph, D 9 kph. We will start the intervals at that speed but increase the speed of the intervals we get into the workout. We encourage runners to choose the group closest to the effort level you want to run at and to keep to the nominal speed for that group to maintain the group dynamic. However if these speeds are significantly too low or high for you then you can choose to run in the group that is closest and then adjust the target speed up to 10% up or down in the game or via the Companion app.

If you have any questions about this event or want to find out more about Zwift Running in general then please visit the Zwift Runners Facebook group or zwift.com/run #gozwiftrun #wow

name: AusCycling Talent Identification
description:
Your journey to the top step starts in your living room.

AusCycling invites you to test yourself against the best. The workout comprises three free ride efforts: 15 seconds, 3 minutes and 12 minutes designed to test your critical power. As with any test or race, ensure you are appropriately warmed up and motivated.

The test is short and sharp, requiring maximum commitment. Erg mode will be turned off during the intervals, you are on your own and its your time to shine.

As you fade through the efforts, use your gears to reduce the resistance and maintain your cadence. Aiming for 90-100rpm for the efforts. Finish the efforts completely spent, the key is to finish all the efforts regardless of how much your power fades or how hard it feels.

Saddle up and enjoy the ride!

 Target Audience;
 16-22yo with no high-performance sport background
 People with vision or physical impairment – any age

People with background in high-performance sport – any age
*If you are outside the ages of 16-22 and have a background in high performance sport or vision/physical impairment please visit https://www.auscycling.org.au/page/virtual-tid and contact us for more information.

name: CC Rider | Social 1.8-2.0 W/kg
description:
Welcome to the CC Riders Afternoon Ride!

Join us for a 60-minute social ride with two pace options. Category D targets 1.8–2.0 W/kg, with riders generally averaging 20 mph or faster. Category E is for riders looking to maintain an average speed below 20 mph. The ride leaders will maintain the advertised efforts, although power and speed may vary slightly with the route, terrain, and draft.

There is no rubber banding or event fence. Settle into your group and enjoy the social pace, or continue ahead if your legs are feeling strong. Drafting is enabled, and late join is available.

All riders comfortable with the advertised pace of their chosen category are welcome.

We ride Monday through Friday at 5:15 PM Eastern Time. Whether you join us occasionally or make it part of your weekday routine, we’d love to see you at the starting line!

Looking for a regular group to ride with? Join CC Riders to stay connected, find upcoming club rides, and get to know your fellow riders. We’re building a friendly group of familiar faces, and there’s always room for another rider.

Join the club:
https://www.zwift.com/clubs/2dce2fec-054a-4b29-a089-28369d430edc/home

Powered by passion. Driven to ride.

name: Chat and roll p/b TBR
description:
Join the TBR crew and roll with Chris Hoiberg for a 45min 2.2 - 2.3 w/kg cruise and chat. Our yellow beacon will average around 40km/h (25mph), consistent with a category C flat ride, with a bit of variation to cater for the majority of riders. Our red beacon may create a second group in the last half of the ride and average around 38km/h (24mph) to help as many riders as possible to finish in a group.

The aim of the ride is to support those wanting to progress from sub 2w/kg rides to something a bit quicker as they improve their strength and fitness. Stronger riders are welcome and your assistance in the group will be appreciated as we will have sweepers working throughout the ride.

So come along at 8.15am AEST each Wednesday and see what makes TBR such a friendly bunch. You're all welcome and you'll have a mighty good time!

We don't use the fence for this ride. All riders should exercise self-control and respect the ride leader by riding with the yellow beacon at all times. Your co-operation helps us provide everyone with a fun, supportive and inclusive ride.

Follow TBR at thebigring.cc to learn more about our events, read ride reports and leave feedback.

name: Old Dog Racing - Masters Tour
description:
Old Dog Racing presents the Masters Tour. A series of shorter and relatively easier races for intermediate level riders.

All races are categorized by age, because to be completely frank, it’s the best racing you can find on Zwift. If you know, you know. And if you don’t you will! Everyone is welcome to race with us, bring some friends and a nemesis or two.

Come and join the fun; A six week tour, Three start times per week, Wednesdays 5:35 pm Eastern; Thursdays 5:35 pm GMT and Fridays 5:35pm Pacific.
Your best finish position each week will count towards your points total.

Races will be mass start and all riders visible, participants will be issued the Zwift Category kit as an aid to identify which category riders you are currently racing against.

The Categories are divided by age as shown below:
A Under 40 (red) B 40-49 (green) C 50-59 (blue) D 60-69 (yellow) and E 70 and over. (purple)

A word of warning; if you haven’t tried age based (masters) racing before, watch out for the yellow and purple jerseys! Those old guys can be surprisingly fast!

Power ups to help you along your way include: The van, the steamroller, the feather, and aero.

Points awarded to each category in every race are: 25, 20,16,13,11,10,9,8,7,6 and 5 very generous participation points!! (You have to finish!). 

Highest accumulated points in each category wins the tour; you’re going to have to wear an HRM and have a Zwift Power account in order to be awarded points.

Overall Tour winner may be eligible to win an Old Dog Racing Mug! (Details on companion club page.).

description:
Come and join the Ascenders as we put on our running shoes and run
daily with our friends too by starting our day in a healthy way. Research
shows that just 30 minutes of running can have huge benefits on your
short-term and long-term health. So we designed our running events to
motivate athletes to run 30 minutes each day to boost your metabolism and
use those calories. Running will also help you look good and feel stronger.

Our group run is designed with runners of all levels in mind and set the
pace range to be determined by our Zwifter Runners. So find a group pace
that matches how you feel each day and make those steps count for you.
Runners who went beyond the event duration will find that we have selected
courses that will help you earn the Route Badges when you run the full
distance.

So lace up those running shoes as everybody is welcome to join with our
friendly and motivating runners.

name: Torturefest | ITT Climbing League | Mountain Mash | Week 2
description:
ITT Climbing League where elevation is the target not distance. The clock runs from Pen to virtual banner finish. The routes have been designed to provide lots of world and climb variations to keep it interesting and challenging.

Week 1 Max Elevation 250 meters
Week 2 Max Elevation 450 meters
Week 3 Max Elevation 650 meters
Week 4 Max Elevation 850 meters
Week 5 when it rarely happens….Alpe Du Zwift

These races are not like the other KOM segment smash races, racing strategy comes to play. You will have to work different power ranges, manage energy levels and ponder bike choices. 
•	No draft regardless of bike.
•	No Power up’s just you and your watts.
•	Weekly distances will fluctuate, for example week 2 could be 15km and week 3 only 10km, elevation is primary focus.
•	Category enforced, must wear HRM.
•	ZwiftPower league in place for weekly and monthly results. Identical setup to zwift power.
•	Some weeks will have long lead-ins to the climb which creates the bike choice dilemma; TT bike, climbing bike or mid race bike change?
•	What is the intensity of your effort on each climb in a week where the course has multiple climbs?
•	How do you regulate your power on the flat sections before or between climbs?  

One week its long drag climbs, next week its multiple smaller climbs…weekly climbing Russian roulette style.

name: Bikealicious Wednesday Worlds
description:
Originating with a group a Zwifters located near Boston, Massachusetts, Wednesday Worlds is a banded/stay together ride open to cyclists and triathletes of all abilities, with novice/intermediate/advanced participants especially welcome. As a stay together (Rubberband) ride, you never will get dropped, ( unless you stop pedaling) thanks to Zwift's banded group ride feature. Ride as hard or as easy as you like, without worry of disrupting the overall ride. The goal of this ride is to provide a supportive opportunity for Zwifters to get together to ride and (if desired) socialize. Courses will vary each week and each ride will run 60 or 90 minutes. If you are looking for a consistent weekly ride with all-around enthusiastic people who are interested in all aspects of cycling, this event might be for you!


Your ride leader has a 40+ year history of top level cycling competition on both the road and track. Additionally, he draws on many years of coaching regional and national level cyclists and his work on aerodynamic testing to provide additional support to ride participants. Questions during the ride are encouraged!

name: Major Taylor 1899 (MT1899) Whirlwind Wednesday
description:
Join us for the Major Taylor 1899 Whirlwind Wednesday!

The ride leader will hold ~2.0 w/kg on the flats for the first 50 minutes to keep the group together. In the final 10 minutes, the fence drops, time to PUSH THE PACE and see who can hang on!

This is a non-banded ride, so maintaining the stated pace is key to staying with the beacon. Please respect group ride etiquette.

Why Major Taylor?

Marshall Walter Taylor, known as “Major Taylor”, was a trailblazing cycling legend. In 1899, he became the first U.S. born African American world champion in any sport, wining the 1-mile and 2-mile sprint world titles, along with multiple national championships.

This ride is hosted by the Major Taylor 1899 (MT1899) community cycling clubs across the USA united to honor his legacy. The acronym after each ride leader’s name identifies the hosting club.

Want to ride IRL with a local Major Taylor club?
https://www.majortaylorassociation.org/friends.shtml

Fun FACT: One of Major Taylor’s nicknames was “The Worcester Whirlwind.”

During the months of May through October there may be rides without an assigned ride leader due to the outdoor riding season. We invite all to connect with us on the social media platforms below to stay in the know:

Complete the ride to earn your Major Taylor Whirlwind Kit

name: Workout Wednesday Run
description:
Join the Zwift Runners for a group run workout that will be of benefit to all distance runners.

The speeds for each group are based on a threshold speed of A group 15 kph, B 13 kph, C 11 kph, D 9 kph. We will start the intervals at that speed but increase the speed of the intervals we get into the workout. We encourage runners to choose the group closest to the effort level you want to run at and to keep to the nominal speed for that group to maintain the group dynamic. However if these speeds are significantly too low or high for you then you can choose to run in the group that is closest and then adjust the target speed up to 10% up or down in the game or via the Companion app.

If you have any questions about this event or want to find out more about Zwift Running in general then please visit the Zwift Runners Facebook group or zwift.com/run #gozwiftrun #wow

name: RollCo: Rolling Tide - 37K
description:
🌊 ROLLING TIDE
Start small. Build big.
Welcome to Rolling Tide — RollCo’s season-long ritual race.

Every week, the distance grows by 1 km.
It begins as a short, explosive opener and steadily evolves into a full-distance endurance epic by year’s end.
This isn’t a one-off event — it’s a shared journey that rises with you.

🏁 Race Format
Rolling Tide is a categorised scratch race.
All riders start together, with categories keeping the racing fair and fast.
The only thing that changes… is the distance.

Week 1 → 1 km
Week 52 → 52 km

Early weeks reward raw power.
Later weeks demand patience, grit, and endurance.
The tide never stops rising.

Rolling Tide is about more than today’s finish line.
It’s about showing up — week after week.
Seeing the same names.
Measuring how far you’ve come as the distance stretches.

You’ll build rivalries.
You’ll track your progress.
You’ll remember the day it all began.

And by the end of the season, everyone who stayed will share the same truth:

“We rode the whole tide together.”

Why Join Rolling Collective?
We’re more than a club — we’re a global community of riders who support each other, grow together, and celebrate every ride, whether it’s a grind, a badge hunt, or a race. Join us on Discord, connect with fellow riders, and be part of something bigger.

Forward, Together

name: Hump Day Ride p/b Team Giant
description:
The Giant Hump Day Ride is two events in one, starting with a moderate effort of 2.6 – 3.0 w/kg. Use this time to warm-up, chat with fellow Zwifters, and maybe decide on a wheel or two you’re ready to get on.

Because this Giant ride gets spicy after the leader announces the start of the After Party: a 20-minute race. Be sure to listen to the ride leader’s instructions, before digging deep. Or not. If you want to keep it casual, it’s all good.

During the After Party the ride leader acts as a sweep, riding with the After Party cruisers, so everyone finishes together.

Complete the Giant Ride, and you’ll automatically unlock the awesome Giant kit! Join in the fun!

name: Mountain Massif structured training:  Break Simulation
description:
Created by Matteo Cigala, from Cigala Cycling, this structured training session is designed to help you cycle at a higher intensity.  For coaching and all your training needs visit https://coaching.cigalacycling.com/trainsmarterridefaster

About the session:
This session targets-controlled intensity changes, short high-power progressions, and aerobic stability. The opening tempo/threshold sets elevate heart rate and prepare the athlete for the progressive 40-second efforts. The progression reps build anaerobic capacity and teach the athlete to accelerate smoothly through increasing power zones. Recovery blocks ensure quality and repeatability. The cool down supports gradual HR reduction and metabolic clearance.
Session details:
Warm Up 
10 min 40–65% CP 100–110 rpm

2 x Sets 3 min @ 80% CP, free cadence 
1 min @ 95% CP, free cadence 
1 min recovery @ 50–60% CP, 100–110 rpm

Recovery
5 min 50–60% CP 100–110 rpm

2 x Sets of 3 x 40s Progressions 
Each rep: 40 seconds steady progression from 105% to 180% CP 
2 min recovery @ 50–60% CP, 100–110 rpm 5 min recovery between sets @ 50–60% CP, 100–110 rpm

Cool Down 
5 min 40–55% CP 100–110 rpm

Total Time: 56 minutes

Key coaching cues:
Control the early intensity changes and keep transitions smooth. Stay relaxed during the tempo and threshold work — avoid overpowering the efforts. Build each 40-second progression gradually, aiming for a clean acceleration rather than a jump. Hold form as power rises: stable core, quiet upper body, smooth pedal stroke. Use the recoveries to reset breathing and cadence so each rep stays high-quality. Keep cadence light and fluid during all recovery blocks. Finish with a calm cool down to bring HR down and support metabolic clearance.

Safety Note: 
Only undertake vigorous exercise if you are fit and healthy to do so. If you are at all unsure, consult a Physician or Doctor first. All training equipment including Bikes and Turbo trainers should be in full working order. Do not use any piece of equipment that does not come up to the required standard.
More information:
For more information check out the Mountain Massif website www.mountainmassif.com, follow on Instagram @mountain_massif, Facebook @mountainmassif and join our Zwift Club, by clicking the following link https://www.zwift.com/clubs/mountainmassif/home
To record all your training data and chart your progress, consider using the TrainingPeaks app or Vekta by following the link https://joinvekta.com/

name: Hincapie Sportswear Power Hour
description: Sweet Spot Training. This workout focuses on (2) 15 minute "sweet spot" intervals, which are at 88-93% of your current FTP. These intervals train your body to resist fatigue during prolonged periods at a power output just below threshold. Over time, you want to move to longer intervals and more total time in zone. Rest intervals will be 5 minutes or less. Total Time in zone: 30 minutes.

name: VietVelo Weekly Social Ride
description: Come join the riders of VietVelo for our weekly social ride. This ride will alternate weeks between an easier social ride (2-2.5 w/kg) for the 1st, 3rd, and 5th Wednesdays to a harder tempo ride (2.5-3 w/kg) for the other weeks. This is a ride NOT a race. If you feel strong, stay in the front and pull. If you feel weak and are looking for a recovery ride, sit in the middle and chat away. Please add VietVelo to the end of your name so we know you are part of the ride. Visit us at vietvelo.org.

name: Workout Wednesday Run
description:
Join the Zwift Runners for a group run workout that will be of benefit to all distance runners.

The speeds for each group are based on a threshold speed of A group 15 kph, B 13 kph, C 11 kph, D 9 kph. We will start the intervals at that speed but increase the speed of the intervals we get into the workout. We encourage runners to choose the group closest to the effort level you want to run at and to keep to the nominal speed for that group to maintain the group dynamic. However if these speeds are significantly too low or high for you then you can choose to run in the group that is closest and then adjust the target speed up to 10% up or down in the game or via the Companion app.

If you have any questions about this event or want to find out more about Zwift Running in general then please visit the Zwift Runners Facebook group or zwift.com/run #gozwiftrun #wow

name: Good Time Riders - Pursuit Race
description:
Also known as Chase races, or Cat and Mouse races, the D category riders will start first, followed by a staggered start for C, B and finally A riders. Keep an eye on the map to see where the other riders are. Who will make it to the finish first? 

You’ll need to work in groups to try and reach the final few kilometres of the race somewhere near the front,  and then it’s all out effort for the overall win. 
 
Good Time Riders (GTR) are a group of Zwifters from across the world who enjoy
riding, training and racing together. We race hard, encourage one another
to be their best, but enjoyment comes first. We have active teams at all
levels racing in Club Ladder, TTT, ZRL and DIRT series. We also run a
regular group rides for the Zwift community on Mondays and Fridays. New members are always very welcome, you can find us on the Companion App, Zwift Clubs, Facebook and Discord.

name: Torturefest | ITT Climbing League | Mountain Mash | Week 2
description:
ITT Climbing League where elevation is the target not distance. The clock runs from Pen to virtual banner finish. The routes have been designed to provide lots of world and climb variations to keep it interesting and challenging.

Week 1 Max Elevation 250 meters
Week 2 Max Elevation 450 meters
Week 3 Max Elevation 650 meters
Week 4 Max Elevation 850 meters
Week 5 when it rarely happens….Alpe Du Zwift

These races are not like the other KOM segment smash races, racing strategy comes to play. You will have to work different power ranges, manage energy levels and ponder bike choices. 
•	No draft regardless of bike.
•	No Power up’s just you and your watts.
•	Weekly distances will fluctuate, for example week 2 could be 15km and week 3 only 10km, elevation is primary focus.
•	Category enforced, must wear HRM.
•	ZwiftPower league in place for weekly and monthly results. Identical setup to zwift power.
•	Some weeks will have long lead-ins to the climb which creates the bike choice dilemma; TT bike, climbing bike or mid race bike change?
•	What is the intensity of your effort on each climb in a week where the course has multiple climbs?
•	How do you regulate your power on the flat sections before or between climbs?  

One week its long drag climbs, next week its multiple smaller climbs…weekly climbing Russian roulette style.

Join us for a 6-week Zwift running league with a different route and distance each week.

Each round awards league points based on your finishing position within your group, with your best 5 results from 6 counting towards the final standings.

Choose your group based on your current 5K average pace:

A – Faster than 4:29 min/km
B – 4:29 to 5:00 min/km
C – 5:00 to 5:46 min/km
D – Slower than 5:46 min/km

Please choose your group honestly. Your group should be based on your normal 5K ability rather than the distance or expected pace of that week's race.  Runners exceeding the group threshold maybe promoted to the faster group in the results.

Autumn League routes:

Week 1 – Makuri Islands – Mech Isle Loop – 4.1 km
Week 2 – New York – Shuman Trail Loop – 2.8 km
Week 3 – Paris – Rues in Rythme – 5.3 km
Week 4 – Watopia – Splash and Dash – 6.2 km
Week 5 – Yorkshire – Queen's Highway – 5.6 km
Week 6 – Scotland – Glasgow Crit Circuit – 3.2 km

The league starts on Thursday 8 October, with events scheduled at 2-hour intervals throughout the day.

After the league is decided, Week 7 is the Queen Stage – a special 10 km mass-start finale.

The Queen Stage does not count towards the league standings. All groups start together for one final race, with overall and group honours up for grabs.

6 scoring rounds. Best 5 count. One 10K Queen Stage finale.

name: Cycle Nation Nightcrawler Ride
description:
Welcome to The Dirty One—the Nightcrawler ride where we trade smooth tarmac for gravel most of the time and embrace a little controlled chaos. We still roll at our signature sub-1.8 w/kg pace, so everyone stays together. But on Thursdays, the route is all about adventure. Expect dusty trails, rolling gravel roads, plenty of laughs, and a crew that’s never afraid to leave the pavement behind. Whether you’re chasing endurance, looking for a social ride, or just want something a little different, The Dirty One delivers. No racing, no pressure, no one gets left behind—just a bunch of Nightcrawlers enjoying the ride.

Gravel routes on Zwift are limited, so every now and then we’ll stick to the roads. But one thing never changes: the relaxed pace, the great company, and the fun that keeps everyone coming back. So grab your bike, bring your sense of adventure, and don’t be afraid to get your virtual tyres dirty. The Nightcrawlers ride together. Thursdays, we ride dirty.

description:

The speeds for each group are based on a threshold speed of A group 15 kph, B 13 kph, C 11 kph, D 9 kph. name: Power Loop
description:
Power Loop”, designed to enhance muscular endurance, cadence control, and
mental resilience. The session is FTP-based and includes motivational cues,
recovery phases, and a final push, making it ideal for riders looking to build
strength and rhythm indoors. 



A circuit of strength and control designed to push your limits and build resilience.




Perfect for developing muscular endurance, rhythm control, and mental toughness. Every loop prepares you for tougher challenges ahead—inside or on the road.



Interval Breakdown:



1. Warm-Up – 10 minutes



3 min in Z1 @ 90 RPM
3 min in Z2 @ 95 RPM
4 min in Z2 @ 100 RPM


2. Main Set – 4 Repeats of This Block (24 minutes total)



Each loop is a mix of tempo, threshold, and VO2 max work with controlled cadence variation:



2 min in Z3 @ 95 RPM — steady sub-threshold push
1 min in Z4 @ 85 RPM — near threshold, slower cadence
1 min in Z5 @ 75 RPM — VO2 max effort, low cadence strength
2 min in Z3 @ 90 RPM — flush with tempo effort
1 min in Z4 @ 100 RPM — FTP effort with fast legs
2 min in Z2 @ 85 RPM — recovery at sweet spot


3. Active Recovery – 5 minutes

5 min in Z1 @ 90 RPM


4. Final Push – 4 minutes

2 min in Z4 @ 90 RPM
2 min in Z5 @ 100 RPM


5. Cool Down – 5 minutes

5 min in Z1 @ 85 RPM

Come and join the Vikings team for some morning fat burning. The aim for this ride is to keep your heart rate and power profile in zone 1 and 2. We encourage all to come fasted for an even better effect. Are you an early morning European zwifter and looking to ride in a fasted state at a pace that works for all, then look no further. If you are from other parts of the world and looking for a short recovery ride, then this will also work perfectly.

For more information about our rides go to: https://www.facebook.com/groups/503388660165279/

name: WTRL Team Time Trial - Zone 1
description:
WTRL Team Time Trial #391

Our weekly WTRL Team Time Trial (TTT) allows teams of 3-8 Zwifters to race against the clock together throughout the day to achieve the fastest possible times. Teams are arranged into WTRL's unique Coffee Classes and feature both women's only Coffee Classes and mixed gender too.
  
 There are 30 racing events and teams can be registered up 30 minutes before each race event starts at www.wtrl.racing/ttt-home/ and you can pick your start time from the available slots. Each team is issued a unique RacePass that must be clicked by each team member to gain access to the event for sign-up. You'll also be able to check out the rules, course records and results which update live throughout the day.
  
 Teams & Riders must be registered with www.WTRL.racing and you'll need to be sharing data, via your Zwift Profile Connections with www.zwiftpower.com.
  
 If you are looking for a team, head to our dedicated WTRL TTT Facebook page where plenty of teams are always happy to welcome guest riders and new team mates (https://www.facebook.com/groups/WTRLTTT). Not on Facebook? Feel free to drop us an email with your preferred WTRL TTT Zone and current Zwift Category 
  
 #wtrl #wtrlttt

name: ZLDR Misty Mornings
description:
Start your day with the serene beauty of Scotland’s iconic misty Loch, all from the comfort of your home. Join us for a peaceful yet invigorating run around the Loch Loop. As the sun rises over the misty waters, feel the calm energy of Scotland’s landscape propel you forward, whether you’re chasing a personal best or simply enjoying the virtual scenery. It’s the perfect way to embrace the early morning and set the tone for a day full of possibilities!

name: EVO CC Vortex Interval Ride [~3-3.8w/kg avg]
description:
Welcome to the Evolution Cycling Club [EVO] interval session. These rides are geared towards Zwifters that are looking for a varied content one hour session that can give them a full 5 zone workout. Draft in the group and stay zone 1-3, or move to the front and join the sprints for zones 4 and 5 for short bursts. Average for this ride will be mid to high Category B but it may vary based upon course/leader. There will be keepers at the back, and they will try hard to save dropped riders. The group is based upon high social interaction so bring your best banter. Use the mobile app or a keyboard to communicate in-ride.

#evo

name: EVO CC Flux Ride [1.8 - 2.0w/kg avg]
description:
This is a Evolution Cycling Club [EVO] Social Event and ride for all. Your co-operation and teamwork is essential to the success of the ride and we ask that all riders respect the pace set by the leader (Yellow Beacon). We may include intervals over and below the ride average advertised power range, but we will allow enough recovery and time to regroup after every effort. This is not a race, so please follow the leader beacon's (Yellow) instructions and if you are feeling strong we would welcome any help offered by stronger riders to bring any dropped riders back to the yellow beacon. We welcome good chat and a social atmosphere for new and experienced Zwifters alike, everyone is welcome.

name: INC Relentless Intervals
description:
Suitable for A riders as a base session, or B & C riders wanting to push themselves.

Examples of the drills are – Z2 with 15sec Z5/6 bursts every 6minutes, alternating Z2/Z3 in various durations, Z2 - Z4 ramps of decreasing duration and many other sessions.

All sessions will be around 60-90mins and will include a warm up so just grab your bottles and head straight to the pen.

This is an Innovation Cycling Training Ride Event – all riders are welcome. These events are put together to push you further than before, if you are feeling fresh hop on the front, if you need rest surf the draft. This training ride is part of the INC RELENTLESS training rides that happen daily with each day focusing on a different area of improvement.

Tips: Use the draft to rest and ensure you do not lose the draft.

name: SZR Early Birdies
description:
Welcome to SZR Early Birdies

This is a group ride with the focus on remaining together. The average pace PRIOR to any race finish will be 2.2 wkg. Sprints and intervals will be added at the discretion of the leader and we will at time ride above and below the advertised pace!

Please regroup quickly after sprints, intervals or hills and sit between the yellow and red beacons.
This ride will particularly benefit D and lower C riders looking to get stronger.

name: 3R Octane Interval Ride [~3.2-3.6 w/kg avg]
description:
This is a 3R Group Ride Event. 3R Octane runs five days a week and is designed to provide a solid and fun training platform for riders.

Different ride leaders target different effort levels and courses, with power averages in the range 3.2-3.8 W/kg.

The wide spread reflects the diversity of rides, including weekly recovery, or transitional, rides which are usually on a Monday. Short, high intensity intervals, longer sweetspot intervals, flying laps, long and short climbs and exploring little used routes all feature.

The rides are typically around an hour long, but some can be up to two hours long, and all end with a mini race.

The Group welcomes rider interaction through messaging and the Octane discord server and features a super bunch of regulars to which newcomers, and riders stepping up from lower intensity rides, are always welcome. We welcome any feedback on our Facebook page https://www.facebook.com/groups/ClubWorldBicycleRelief/

#Team3R #Ride3R #RideRaceRaise #3r

name: 3R VOLT Interval Ride [~2.6-3.2 w/kg avg]
description:
This is a 3R Group Ride so please follow the leader beacon's (Yellow) instructions and if you are feeling strong, please help the keeper beacon (Red) to assist other riders back to the pack. 3R VOLT runs five days a week and is designed to provide a solid and fun training platform for riders.

Different ride leaders target different effort levels and courses, with power averages in the range 2.8-3.2 w/kg.

The wide spread reflects the diversity of rides and training needs, the following is a typical week:
Monday – After what has hopefully been a fun backed weekend on the bike, this our recovery session
Tuesday – Tends to be more of a classic interval session, riders usually finish with an average of around 3.0w/kg
Wednesday – We take to the hills and one of our tougher sessions with riders averaging around 3.2w/kg
Thursday – is our no red beacon ride and again tough interval sets and riders finishing around 3.2w/kg
Friday - is a little different, we don't take ourselves too seriously and often play a variety of games and quizzes along side the intervals and riders end up with around 2.8-3.0w/kg

The rides are typically around an hour long, but some may take up to 75mins with the majority finishing with either a ramp or a mini race.

The group welcomes rider interaction through messaging and the VOLT discord server and features a friendly bunch of regulars to which newcomers, and riders stepping up from lower intensity rides, are always welcome. We welcome any feedback on our Facebook page https://www.facebook.com/groups/ClubWorldBicycleRelief/

This group ride is not a race so. We welcome any feedback on our Facebook page https://www.facebook.com/groups/ClubWorldBicycleRelief/ #Team3R #Ride3R #RideRaceRaise.

name: NPRC - Run Every Day Powered By NoblePro
description:
Come and join the fastest growing running club on Zwift.  With a choice of 5 or 10k you can pick your distance. Whether you are a beginner or experienced runner come and join us, you can run at whatever pace you like, it’s not a race unless you want it to be!

name: 3R SPARK Interval Ride [~2.2-2.5 w/kg avg]
description: This is a 3R Group Ride Event (not a race). 3R Spark runs five days a week and is designed to be an accessible and sociable training session, aimed primarily at riders is Cat-D. Different ride leaders target different effort levels and courses, with power averages in the range 2.0-2.5 W/kg. The wide spread reflects the diversity of rides. Mondays and Tuesdays are our entry-level steady-state rides, where we aim to hold a steady 2.0-2.2 throughout. Wednesdays are a steady recovery ride, where we split into two different ability groups. Thursdays and Fridays are our interval sessions, designed to help Cat D riders push themselves a little further. For interval sessions we aim to average between 2.2-2.5 for the session, but there will be times above and below. Thursday and Friday sessions often include an optional mini-race at the end. Rides are typically around an hour long. Spark is a great introduction to group rides on Zwift, we are a friendly and supportive group who love to see one another succeed. We always have a sweeper (red beacon) whose wheel you can grab if you get dropped. There’s always plenty of good chat, via in-ride messages or on Discord. Come and join us! Join the 3R Facebook group for more info: https://www.facebook.com/groups/ClubWorldBicycleRelief/ #Team3R #3R #RideRaceRaise

name: GXY SURGE
description:
EVENT DESCRIPTION

Part of the SURGE group of events, Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday at the same time.  

This event brings a different workout structure each of the four days of the week.  This may include power pyramids, intervals and chase strategies.  Expect a fun social event where sprints and Kom segments may be included.

EVENT DYNAMICS

Category    - D

Power 	    - 1.6 > 2.5wkg but expect the event to finish around 2.1wkg based on a 75kg rider.

Fence 	    - Will be set to KICK! used at the leader's discretion

Draft	    - Enabled – focus required to stay within the group

Sweeper     - Yes! Red beacon and beacon support riders will have a GXY tag after their name

ETHOS 

We at GXY are committed to creating a culture of belonging, inclusivity and compassion empowering people to grow stronger, work together and support one another to achieve shared success on Zwift

GXY – Here together, for you 💜

If you want to become a member and join our community to race, ride socially, or both, please come and join ideally via our Facebook link:

https://www.facebook.com/groups/galaxycyclingclub/
https://www.strava.com/clubs/989894
https://www.instagram.com/galaxycyclingclub

name: Endure IQ Training Squad Session
description:
SESSION FOCUS:
The focus of this session is to spend as much time as possible at and above
~90% of your VO2max. The priority is on maintaining high power/pace during the
work intervals. These sessions are highly stressful but great for generating
adaptations that will improve your oxygen-carrying capacity and therefore top-
end aerobic capacity. For long-distance triathletes, these sessions can also
serve as an effective precursor to longer interval sessions.

WARM-UP:
Progressive for 20 min
PREP SET:
5 x 30 sec at L5/30 sec at L1
2 min Recovery
MAIN SET:
Sets of 30-sec reps at L5, 30 sec at L1 (5 min recovery between sets)
COOLDOWN:
10 min

name: Run in the Park Autumn Run League - Week 2
description:
IMPORTANT: You must be registered with ZwiftPower for your result to be included in the official Run in the Park results at www.runinthepark.co.uk

Run in the Park Autumn Run League 2026

Join us for a 6-week Zwift running league with a different route and distance each week.

Each round awards league points based on your finishing position within your group, with your best 5 results from 6 counting towards the final standings.

Choose your group based on your current 5K average pace:

A – Faster than 4:29 min/km
B – 4:29 to 5:00 min/km
C – 5:00 to 5:46 min/km
D – Slower than 5:46 min/km

Please choose your group honestly. Your group should be based on your normal 5K ability rather than the distance or expected pace of that week's race.  Runners exceeding the group threshold maybe promoted to the faster group in the results.

Autumn League routes:

Week 1 – Makuri Islands – Mech Isle Loop – 4.1 km
Week 2 – New York – Shuman Trail Loop – 2.8 km
Week 3 – Paris – Rues in Rythme – 5.3 km
Week 4 – Watopia – Splash and Dash – 6.2 km
Week 5 – Yorkshire – Queen's Highway – 5.6 km
Week 6 – Scotland – Glasgow Crit Circuit – 3.2 km

The league starts on Thursday 8 October, with events scheduled at 2-hour intervals throughout the day.

After the league is decided, Week 7 is the Queen Stage – a special 10 km mass-start finale.

The Queen Stage does not count towards the league standings. All groups start together for one final race, with overall and group honours up for grabs.

6 scoring rounds. Best 5 count. One 10K Queen Stage finale.

description:
This is a social ride welcoming all riders. Our mission is to push you further than before, build your endurance, and have fun. If you are feeling strong, push to the front and drag the group; if not, just sit in the peloton.

description:

Join the MAAP crew each week, we’ll roll as a group at a moderate 2-2.5 w/kg pace. The course varies each week, with a range of undulating routes. name: Torturefest | ITT Climbing League | Mountain Mash | Week 2
description:
ITT Climbing League where elevation is the target not distance. The clock runs from Pen to virtual banner finish. The routes have been designed to provide lots of world and climb variations to keep it interesting and challenging.

Week 1 Max Elevation 250 meters
Week 2 Max Elevation 450 meters
Week 3 Max Elevation 650 meters
Week 4 Max Elevation 850 meters
Week 5 when it rarely happens….Alpe Du Zwift

These races are not like the other KOM segment smash races, racing strategy comes to play. You will have to work different power ranges, manage energy levels and ponder bike choices. 
•	No draft regardless of bike.
•	No Power up’s just you and your watts.
•	Weekly distances will fluctuate, for example week 2 could be 15km and week 3 only 10km, elevation is primary focus.
•	Category enforced, must wear HRM.
•	ZwiftPower league in place for weekly and monthly results. Identical setup to zwift power.
•	Some weeks will have long lead-ins to the climb which creates the bike choice dilemma; TT bike, climbing bike or mid race bike change?
•	What is the intensity of your effort on each climb in a week where the course has multiple climbs?
•	How do you regulate your power on the flat sections before or between climbs?  

One week its long drag climbs, next week its multiple smaller climbs…weekly climbing Russian roulette style.

name: Team Italy Spicy Coffee Italian Ride
description:
Se cerchi la giusta compagnia per prepararti al fine settimana sei nel posto giusto.
Lo scopo della SPICY COFFEE ITALIAN RIDE è quello di stare tutti insieme, sfruttare la scia del gruppo e fare due chiacchiere ad un ritmo medio fra i 2.0 e i 2.5 w/kg per 90 minuti, il late join è attivo per 30 minuti.
Questa NON è una gara.
Segui le istruzioni dei leader(giallo) per un gruppo compatto.
Ricordati di non superare la fence (barra rossa) altrimenti verrai eliminato.
Partecipa a questa ride per sbloccare la divisa del team italy.
BUONA PEDALATA A TUTTI
TEAM ITALY organizza una vasta gamma di eventi, tutti con le seguenti regole:
-in una pedalata di categoria D, alcuni ciclisti sono principianti, segui le istruzioni del
leader (logo giallo) che appaiono come testo al centro e tieni presente che il ritmo sarà fra i 2.0 e i 2.5 w/kg
-Il valore w/kg sarà diverso per tutti voi, il motivo principale sarà il peso, seguito dalla
capacità di utilizzare la scia e l'equipaggiamento della vostra bici in gioco
-abilitare i messaggi nelle opzioni zwift, fondamentali per una buona esperienza
-le pedalate della categoria D sono facili per un ciclista con C alto, 3w/kg ftp, impegnative per un C basso, 2.5 w/kg ftp, estreme per un ciclista D con 2 w/kg FTP, lo stesso per le
corse C, facili per un A, 4w/kg ftp, impegnative per B 3.2 w/kg ftp, ed estreme per C con 2.5
w/kg ftp.


Are you looking for the perfect companion and you are training for the weekend? This is the right place.
Spicy Coffee Italian Ride's goal is to stay together, enjoy the group draft, and have a bit of easy chat at an average pace between 2.0 and 2.5 w/kg for 90 minutes, late join is enabled for 30 minutes.
This is NOT A RACE.


Follow the leaders' instructions (yellow beacons) to keep the group tight.
Remember the Fence is KILLER, 60 seconds over and you'll be out of the event.
Join this ride to unlock the Team Italy Jersey.
TEAM ITALY organizes a wide range of events, which all agree to the following rules:
- in a D category ride, some riders are beginners, and follow the leader's instructions (yellow
beacon) that appear as text in the middle and keep in mind that the pace will be between 2.0 and 2.5 w/kg


-The w/kg value will be different for all of you, the main reason will be weight, followed by the
capacity to use the draft and your in-game bike equipment
- enable the messages in Zwift options, fundamental for a great experience
- D category's rides are easy for a high C rider, 3wkg ftp, challenging for a low C, 2.5 w/kg
FTP, is extreme for a D rider with 2 w/kg FTP, same for C rides, easy for an A, 4 w/kg ftp,
challenging for B's, 3.2 w/kg ftp, and extreme for C's 2.5 w/kg ftp.
- if you have any suggestions please let us know

name: PAOLO BARBERA & SCANNELLATORI SERIALI WORKOUT
description:
"Scannellatori Seriali" is a large community of cyclists, triathletes, and runners. We invite you to join our community by following our Instagram page at https://www.instagram.com/scannellatori_seriali/ or contacting us on Facebook.
 
Coach Paolo Barbera (Please visit www.heycoach.it )   is a Certified Triathlon and Ironman Coach and the founder of Active Kids, a sporting clinic to help children and adults in the prevention and treatment of obesity through healty nutrition and tailored training programs

Paolo is an experienced thriathlete and cyclist, in 2017 opened an endurance training center in milan, Tri60, specilized in indoor training.

In the last ten years Paolo has developed training programs for triathletes, runners and cyclists. Indoor training plays a key role to control pace, cadence and mental strenght.

Paolo’s workouts are designed to mix different training zones aiming to maximize results in a very short time. Paolo’s coachees by following his workouts, at the right intensity, have achieved challenging results.

name: Run in the Park Autumn Run League - Week 2
description:
IMPORTANT: You must be registered with ZwiftPower for your result to be included in the official Run in the Park results at www.runinthepark.co.uk

Run in the Park Autumn Run League 2026

Join us for a 6-week Zwift running league with a different route and distance each week.

Each round awards league points based on your finishing position within your group, with your best 5 results from 6 counting towards the final standings.

Choose your group based on your current 5K average pace:

A – Faster than 4:29 min/km
B – 4:29 to 5:00 min/km
C – 5:00 to 5:46 min/km
D – Slower than 5:46 min/km

Please choose your group honestly. Your group should be based on your normal 5K ability rather than the distance or expected pace of that week's race.  Runners exceeding the group threshold maybe promoted to the faster group in the results.

Autumn League routes:

Week 1 – Makuri Islands – Mech Isle Loop – 4.1 km
Week 2 – New York – Shuman Trail Loop – 2.8 km
Week 3 – Paris – Rues in Rythme – 5.3 km
Week 4 – Watopia – Splash and Dash – 6.2 km
Week 5 – Yorkshire – Queen's Highway – 5.6 km
Week 6 – Scotland – Glasgow Crit Circuit – 3.2 km

The league starts on Thursday 8 October, with events scheduled at 2-hour intervals throughout the day.

After the league is decided, Week 7 is the Queen Stage – a special 10 km mass-start finale.

The Queen Stage does not count towards the league standings. All groups start together for one final race, with overall and group honours up for grabs.

6 scoring rounds. Best 5 count. One 10K Queen Stage finale.

description:
Welcome to [ASC] - Ascenders Brunch Bunch for a chilled Rubber Banded ride around the virtual roads of Zwift.  Each week the course will vary so whether you’re a beginner just starting out on your first group rides, this is a great way to start. If recovering from injury, or just looking for a steady paced ride then come and join us. We aim to provide a safe encouraging ride for you to enjoy. You’ll be very welcome in the Brunch Bunch


This is a banded group ride and not a race. As long as you keep spinning you will stay with the group. If you’re looking for an easy ride then sit in the group near the Yellow Lead Beacon. However if you’re feeling strong then head to the front and help pull the group along.


Please note this ride is not fenced.

name: WTRL Team Time Trial - Zone 7
description:
WTRL Team Time Trial #391

Our weekly WTRL Team Time Trial (TTT) allows teams of 3-8 Zwifters to race against the clock together throughout the day to achieve the fastest possible times. Teams are arranged into WTRL's unique Coffee Classes and feature both women's only Coffee Classes and mixed gender too.
  
 There are 30 racing events and teams can be registered up 30 minutes before each race event starts at www.wtrl.racing/ttt-home/ and you can pick your start time from the available slots. Each team is issued a unique RacePass that must be clicked by each team member to gain access to the event for sign-up. name: The Chop by AHDR
description:
AHDR THE CHOP

Being "in the chop" is an Aussie expression that you won't read about in the UCI rulebook. It's one of the many nuances of bike racing that only comes with experience.

Sometimes when you're in a race and find yourself in the final break-away bunch you might get asked "are we in the chop?" or "are we chopping it?". This is referring to collusion between the lead riders to work together until the finish. Many times a break-away will be doomed in the final kilometres because everyone starts playing cat and mouse, attacking, sitting up, etc.

But all that goes out the window in the last lap. This is generally where the group comes together and the final push begins. Working together goes out the window and is every man or woman for themselves for the final sprint to the line.

AHDR The Chop is a flat fast time-based handicap race. Do you always get blown out the back on the start of a multi grade race trying to hang onto the guy going with A grade pushing 5w/kg. Well not on The Chop. Released in Grades there are time splits from D to A with the intention of all coming together at the end for the big finish. Each Grade wears a different AHDR/Zwift kit making each grade easily identifiable on who's wheel you want to catch if they go past.

Races happen on Thursday evenings. We plan to add further races in the future. No single race has been the same. Many variables are at play on The Chop including course (which is generally a flat course), race numbers, and the inevitable sandbaggers. It has been called a team time trail and cat and mouse but the real racers know it only as "THE CHOP". Do you have what it takes to take the glory?

A Grade – AHDR GIANT Kit
B Grade – HDR Kit
C Grade – Fluoro Pink
D Grade – Fluoro Camo

name: Run in the Park Autumn Run League - Week 2
description:
IMPORTANT: You must be registered with ZwiftPower for your result to be included in the official Run in the Park results at www.runinthepark.co.uk

Run in the Park Autumn Run League 2026

Join us for a 6-week Zwift running league with a different route and distance each week.

Each round awards league points based on your finishing position within your group, with your best 5 results from 6 counting towards the final standings.

Choose your group based on your current 5K average pace:

A – Faster than 4:29 min/km
B – 4:29 to 5:00 min/km
C – 5:00 to 5:46 min/km
D – Slower than 5:46 min/km

Please choose your group honestly. Your group should be based on your normal 5K ability rather than the distance or expected pace of that week's race.  Runners exceeding the group threshold maybe promoted to the faster group in the results.

Autumn League routes:

Week 1 – Makuri Islands – Mech Isle Loop – 4.1 km
Week 2 – New York – Shuman Trail Loop – 2.8 km
Week 3 – Paris – Rues in Rythme – 5.3 km
Week 4 – Watopia – Splash and Dash – 6.2 km
Week 5 – Yorkshire – Queen's Highway – 5.6 km
Week 6 – Scotland – Glasgow Crit Circuit – 3.2 km

The league starts on Thursday 8 October, with events scheduled at 2-hour intervals throughout the day.

After the league is decided, Week 7 is the Queen Stage – a special 10 km mass-start finale.

name: CRYO-GEN: The Tempo Split
description:
Push your limits, find your rhythm.
Welcome to The Tempo Split, a dynamic tempo session designed to help you build aerobic power and endurance. This isn’t just a group ride; it’s a choose-your-own-adventure workout where you decide how deep to dig.

How it Works
We all start together in a single pen for a 10-20 minute progressive warm-up at a controlled, social pace. Once the warm-up is complete, the “Split” begins.
The Yellow Beacon (Lead): Will begin intervals at a high-tempo pace of 3.2 – 3.5 w/kg. This is for those looking to challenge their sustained power.
The Red Beacon (Sweep): Will begin intervals at a steady tempo pace of 2.7 – 3.0 w/kg. This is the safety net for those who want a solid workout without going “into the red.”

The Challenge
Start with the Yellow Beacon. Your goal is to hold that higher intensity for as long as possible. If the effort becomes unsustainable or your heart rate climbs too high, don’t worry—simply ease back to the Red Beacon following behind and finish the interval with that group.

Course & Intensity Notes
Please note that this is a flexible training session:
Terrain Impact: The ride format and group cohesion may change based on the route’s profile. Expect paces to shift slightly on climbs or descents.
Variable Intervals: Interval intensity and duration are subject to change week-to-week based on the specific goals of the session and the total distance of the chosen course.

Pro Tip: Use the draft! Whether you’re with the Yellow or Red group, staying tucked in a pack will help you maintain these tempo zones more efficiently.
Pro Tip: Keep an eye on the on-screen chat. The Beacons will announce interval starts, finishes, and any adjustments to the target w/kg based on the terrain.

Ride Rules
Be Kind: This is a supportive training environment.
Listen to your body: There is no shame in dropping back to the Red Beacon; that’s exactly why it’s there!
Stay Predictable: Avoid sudden surges so the groups can stay formed.

ZWTC is your community for fun and fitness. name: DWGZ — Hollentour
description:
DWGZ — Höllentour

Welcome to DWGZ (Determined Witty Gritty Zwifters) — a global crew of cyclists who show up with grit, humor, heart, and the kind of energy that lifts the whole group. Many of us have zwifted together for years, and some have taken those virtual connections IRL, organizing meetups around the world. DWGZ builds more than fitness — we build community, emotional endurance, and the kind of camaraderie that makes even the hardest efforts feel lighter through shared suffering.

Höllentour — hell tour, German-style — is our Thursday ride with teeth. It's a step up from a standard endurance spin, with some real climbing worked in to keep the legs honest. This ride brings the heat early in the week without going full suffer-fest — just enough vert to earn your Thursday.

Whether you're building climbing strength, chasing a harder effort before the weekend, or just want to ride with people who'll push you and laugh with you at the same time, this one's for you.

Ride Categories 🚴 B Category – 3.2–4.0 w/kg 🚴 C Category – 2.8–3.2 w/kg 🚴 D Category – 2.0–2.6 w/kg

Expect steady climbing pressure, smooth rotation, and a welcoming group from yellow beacon to sweep. Every pocket of the ride is built on teamwork, connection, and that signature DWGZ vibe.

DWGZ rides run seven days a week at 6:05 AM Eastern (US) — each one an opportunity to build strength, connection, and global community.
Clip in, turn up the heat, and ride through the Höllentour with us.

name: Know No Bounds Ride
description:
Welcome to the #KnowNoBounds Ride! A ride where we explore the boundaries (or lack thereof) on Zwift.
The ride will begin with 30 minutes at 3 w/kg, utilizing the fence to keep riders together. At the end of the 30 minutes, riders are free to do as they please:
they can stay together and explore the chosen course for the day, or they can head off to the nearest mountain with friends and race it!

When the 30 minute "fenced" portion of the ride is over, we will #KnowNoBounds. Have bike, will travel.
If needed, you will be able to turn to ride in opposite direction on the circuit to reconnect with the group quicker (if you need restroom or are dropped),
and most importantly, the group is not limited to the in-game courses. We can choose to go up a mountain, along a riverside, or any road we want to!

We’re on a mission: to set everyday cyclists free to explore without limits. And we’re going by bike.

Community and camaraderie in cycling is everything: group chat on this ride is highly encouraged!

name: WTRL Team Time Trial - Zone 11
description:
WTRL Team Time Trial #391

Our weekly WTRL Team Time Trial (TTT) allows teams of 3-8 Zwifters to race against the clock together throughout the day to achieve the fastest possible times. Teams are arranged into WTRL's unique Coffee Classes and feature both women's only Coffee Classes and mixed gender too.

name: Run in the Park Autumn Run League - Week 2
description:
IMPORTANT: You must be registered with ZwiftPower for your result to be included in the official Run in the Park results at www.runinthepark.co.uk

Run in the Park Autumn Run League 2026

Join us for a 6-week Zwift running league with a different route and distance each week.

Each round awards league points based on your finishing position within your group, with your best 5 results from 6 counting towards the final standings.

Choose your group based on your current 5K average pace:

A – Faster than 4:29 min/km
B – 4:29 to 5:00 min/km
C – 5:00 to 5:46 min/km
D – Slower than 5:46 min/km

Please choose your group honestly. Your group should be based on your normal 5K ability rather than the distance or expected pace of that week's race.  Runners exceeding the group threshold maybe promoted to the faster group in the results.

Autumn League routes:

Week 1 – Makuri Islands – Mech Isle Loop – 4.1 km
Week 2 – New York – Shuman Trail Loop – 2.8 km
Week 3 – Paris – Rues in Rythme – 5.3 km
Week 4 – Watopia – Splash and Dash – 6.2 km
Week 5 – Yorkshire – Queen's Highway – 5.6 km
Week 6 – Scotland – Glasgow Crit Circuit – 3.2 km

The league starts on Thursday 8 October, with events scheduled at 2-hour intervals throughout the day.

After the league is decided, Week 7 is the Queen Stage – a special 10 km mass-start finale.

The Queen Stage does not count towards the league standings. All groups start together for one final race, with overall and group honours up for grabs.

6 scoring rounds. Best 5 count. One 10K Queen Stage finale.

name: SROZ's Contenders, Pretenders, & Rear-Enders
description:
Whether you’re a Tour de France hopeful, a procrastinating amateur, or the person whose front tire spends a suspicious amount of time in someone else’s rear derailleur...we honestly don't care!

There are no "real" awards for winning a climb or clinching a sprint. If you’re looking for a trophy, try a middle school soccer tournament.

The goal is to maintain a steady engine...smooth rotations and clean pulls. Even when the profile gets punchy or the wind shifts, we're staying "dialed in" on 18–20 mph (30–32 kph).

Feeling a little gapped? Don't sweat it. We strive to have a dedicated sweeper on every ride to help pull you back into the fold.

The "Gene Autry" Philosophy: We believe in freedom! As the legend himself said, we won’t fence you in.

At the end of the day, you’re the captain of your own bike. Whether you’re pushing the pace or soaking in the scenery: ride your ride!

So come out, enjoy the virtual fresh air, and keep the faith!

eventSubgroups.name: SROZ's Contenders, Pretenders, & Rear-Enders (D)
eventSubgroups.description:
We don’t care if you’re a contender, pretender, or rear-ender!  We just enjoy riding with others in a fun, social group. 

There are no “real” awards for being first on a climb or on a sprint during our rides, only the satisfaction of being able to ride a bike for just one more day! 

The pace may vary depending on the course, but we will strive to ride and socialize with an overall average pace of approximately 18-20mph (30-32kph).  

We will try to have a sweeper on each ride to help any rider who may want to return to the group. 

Also, we will be applying the Gene Autry philosophy…we won’t fence you in!

Remember, the choice is yours…ride your ride!

So, enjoy your ride, keep the faith, and become that someone!

name: Hercules - The Thursday Social

name: Zwift Women's Training Club Workout
description:
Welcome to the Zwift Women’s Training Club workouts! 

ZWTC is your community for fun and fitness. Our weekly workouts will take you through some of Zwift’s most popular training plans, and with the flexibility to join in any time, regardless of where we are in the plan! Get the most out of your Zwifting with training designed by world-class coaches, like 3x Olympic Gold medalist, Kristin Armstrong!

The group workouts will be held every 3 hours UTC on Tuesdays and Thursdays. We’ll also offer recovery rides every 3 hours on Wednesdays - be on the look out for special guests joining those! Our main goal is to provide you with a consistent experience week in and week out, to challenge yourself in a supportive group setting, making friends and getting fit along the way! 

Join the Zwift Women’s Training Club to connect with new ride friends, ask questions, and get advice from experts.  https://www.zwift.com/clubs/ZwiftWTC/join

Love these workouts? Check out the club for more opportunities to train with us! We offer social rides every 3 hours on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays in addition to the Tuesday/Thursday workouts.

name: Thursday Pizza Burner  🍕🔥
description:
This week's ride unlocks the H2O Audio headphones in game. Like the look? The sound is great, too! Pick up a real-life set at https://zwiftinsider.com/h2o, using discount code ZWIFTINSIDER for 20% off.

Each week we spin through 100km of pristine Zwift roads, rotating between flattish routes to keep the endurance training fast and fun. Burn those pizza slices, chat about all things Zwift/cycling, and build your base with ride leader Eric Schlange, creator of Zwift Insider!

PACE:
Eric will ride at ~2.5w/kg/210W for an average speed of 37-39kph (23-24mph). Join his yellow beacon group to ride at the stated pace, join the "zinners" up the road for something spicier, or do whatever keeps you motivated.

VOICE CHAT:
Longer rides always pass faster with voice chat, so join us on Discord if you're able! Find us at https://discord.gg/zwiftinsider

UNLOCK THE KIT:
You will unlock the Zwift Insider kit upon finishing this event.

name: Outseason Thursdays with Endurance Nation
description:
Transform Your Winter with Endurance Nation’s OutSeason Program!

Get ready to build next-level fitness with our 9-week OutSeason cycling series! Join us every Tuesday and Thursday for a focused, one-hour session designed to boost your strength, endurance, and power. With just two workouts per week, you’ll start building winter strength that will prepare you to reach your goals next season. This program is tried-and-true, with over 10,000 athletes using it to succeed in cycling and triathlon for over 16 years.

Why settle for base miles alone when you can add targeted intensity this winter? Join Endurance Nation and see what a season of smart training can do. Discover more about the OutSeason at www.endurancenation.us/zwift.

Love these workouts? Check out the club for more opportunities to train with us! We offer social rides on Saturdays, Sundays and Mondays each week — they are great alternates to these scheduled workouts!

name: EMU Japan Race
description:
(Japanese follows) 
Welcome to the EMU Japan Race! POWER UPs:Allowed at all times BIKES:All allowed CATEGORY: Use your FTP and then divide by your weight in kg then pick the correct group: A:4.0 W/kg FTP+ B:3.2 W/kg to 4.0 W/kg FTP C:2.5 W/kg to 3.1 W/kg FTP D:Under 2.4 W/kg FTP ROUTE: CHAMPS-ELYSEES 6.60km(1lap) Have Fun! Ride On!!

EMU Japan Race 毎週火/木曜日に開催するEMU公式レース!!
EMUで人気のあるコースを中心に選択。
コースは毎週変わります！
Zwifterの参加をお待ちしています。
POWER UPs:アイテム使用可能 BIKES:全ての自転車を選択可能 カテゴリーに関して あなたのFTPを体重で割った数値をパワーウエイトレシオ【○○W/kg】となります。
例：FTP250W、体重60kgの方は4.166W/kgになりますのでAカテゴリーを選択下さい。
FTPとはサイクリストが1時間を通して維持できるパワーになります。 FTPの数値がわからない方はZwift Workout内のFTPテストで計測出来ます。
A:4.0W/kg FTP以上の方
B:3.2W/kg～4.0W/kg FTPの方
C:2.5W/kg～3.1W/kg FTPの方
D:2.4W/kg FTP以下の方
Have Fun! Ride On!! #EMU Speed Club #ZwiftJapan

name: Tower 26 Group Workout
description:
TOWER 26 Workout: Happy Fun Time

This weeks Tower 26 workout focuses on tempo designed to get you riding FAST and STRONG!

Join EVERY Tuesday and Thursday on Zwift while being COACHED on Zoom. Subscribe to the monthly workouts here.

https://training.tower26.com/t-26-cycling-training-program

TOWER 26 Swimming, the premiere name in triathlon swim training, is now offering triathlon coaching services. Led by experienced Head Coach Jim Lubinski, these triathlon specific cycling workouts will follow the TOWER 26 season-long progression of phases of training building your cycling strength in a smart, periodized manner. Our phases of training entail: Foundation, Sharpening, Race Preparation, Race Ready, and Recovery/Technical. Each workout will fit within the current phase of training, educating the athlete as to how the specific workout fits into the overall season-long progression and how the workout will best get the athlete Performance Prepared and Race READY.

Listen to the TOWER 26 - Be Race Ready Podcast with Coach Jim Lubinski and Coach Gerry Rodrigues help further your triathlon education in an entertaining spin on it.

For more information on TOWER 26 go to www.TOWER26.com or email

name: WTRL Team Time Trial - Zone 12
description:
WTRL Team Time Trial #391

Our weekly WTRL Team Time Trial (TTT) allows teams of 3-8 Zwifters to race against the clock together throughout the day to achieve the fastest possible times. Teams are arranged into WTRL's unique Coffee Classes and feature both women's only Coffee Classes and mixed gender too.
  
 There are 30 racing events and teams can be registered up 30 minutes before each race event starts at www.wtrl.racing/ttt-home/ and you can pick your start time from the available slots. Each team is issued a unique RacePass that must be clicked by each team member to gain access to the event for sign-up. You'll also be able to check out the rules, course records and results which update live throughout the day.
  
 Teams & Riders must be registered with www.WTRL.racing and you'll need to be sharing data, via your Zwift Profile Connections with www.zwiftpower.com.
  
 If you are looking for a team, head to our dedicated WTRL TTT Facebook page where plenty of teams are always happy to welcome guest riders and new team mates (https://www.facebook.com/groups/WTRLTTT). Not on Facebook? Feel free to drop us an email with your preferred WTRL TTT Zone and current Zwift Category 
  
 #wtrl #wtrlttt

name: Virginia's Blue Ridge TWENTY28 Road to LA
description:
Virginia’s Blue Ridge TWENTY28 are now in our 20th year of operation developing high-performance athletes and the next generation of competitive cyclists. Success in aligning student-athletes with college scholarships through cycling. Support of the multi-discipline athlete. Adaptive, dynamic, versatile, resilient, and committed to growing diversity in the landscape of women’s cycling.

When the team was formed in 2005, The goal of TWENTY12 was to create a pathway for athletes to the 2012 London Olympics. London resulted in two Olympic medals; gold and silver, the only U.S based road program to achieve this. The team replicated its success with 5 medals in Rio 2016 Olympics/Paralympics, two in Tokyo, two in Paris 2024, and now on to LA 2028.

Ride Leaders + Sweepers include
Amanda Coker who is a level 100 Zwifter and is an accomplished ultra-endurance IRL athlete: World Record Holder - 86,573.2 miles ridden in a year - yes that’s riding 237 miles per day for 365 straight days

Sweepers include members of Virginia’s Blue Ridge TWENTY24 Pro Cycling and regulars are team founder Nicola Cranmer and TWENTY24 eSports captain Kristin Kulchinsky

Find us on social media
Web: http://teamtwenty24.com/
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/twenty28procycling/
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/twenty24procycling

To join our club, please follow the link provided: https://www.zwift.com/clubs/5b278b37-bb5c-41fd-9834-cde077342a0c/home

description:

name: Run in the Park Autumn Run League - Week 2
description:
IMPORTANT: You must be registered with ZwiftPower for your result to be included in the official Run in the Park results at www.runinthepark.co.uk

Run in the Park Autumn Run League 2026

Join us for a 6-week Zwift running league with a different route and distance each week.

Each round awards league points based on your finishing position within your group, with your best 5 results from 6 counting towards the final standings.

Choose your group based on your current 5K average pace:

A – Faster than 4:29 min/km
B – 4:29 to 5:00 min/km
C – 5:00 to 5:46 min/km
D – Slower than 5:46 min/km

Please choose your group honestly. Your group should be based on your normal 5K ability rather than the distance or expected pace of that week's race.  Runners exceeding the group threshold maybe promoted to the faster group in the results.

Autumn League routes:

Week 1 – Makuri Islands – Mech Isle Loop – 4.1 km
Week 2 – New York – Shuman Trail Loop – 2.8 km
Week 3 – Paris – Rues in Rythme – 5.3 km
Week 4 – Watopia – Splash and Dash – 6.2 km
Week 5 – Yorkshire – Queen's Highway – 5.6 km
Week 6 – Scotland – Glasgow Crit Circuit – 3.2 km

The league starts on Thursday 8 October, with events scheduled at 2-hour intervals throughout the day.

After the league is decided, Week 7 is the Queen Stage – a special 10 km mass-start finale.

The Queen Stage does not count towards the league standings. All groups start together for one final race, with overall and group honours up for grabs.

6 scoring rounds. Best 5 count. One 10K Queen Stage finale.

What is Racing Score?

Racing Score is an intuitive system that replaces the traditional categories (A - D) with a 0-1000 scale to reflect your current level, considering various metrics like race performances and power. This score helps Zwift recommend the most competitive band to race in, ensuring a fun, rewarding, and exciting experience as you track your progression throughout your Zwift racing adventures.

WHAT IS ZWIFT POWER? For further information on connecting to Zwift Power check out this support page: https://support.zwift.com/en_us/connecting-to-zwiftpower-SyldRc_4H

description:
Welcome to the Zwift Women’s Training Club workouts! 

ZWTC is your community for fun and fitness. Our weekly workouts will take you through some of Zwift’s most popular training plans, and with the flexibility to join in any time, regardless of where we are in the plan! Get the most out of your Zwifting with training designed by world-class coaches, like 3x Olympic Gold medalist, Kristin Armstrong!

Our main goal is to provide you with a consistent experience week in and week out, to challenge yourself in a supportive group setting, making friends and getting fit along the way!

name: Applewood Cycling Group Ride
description:
Established in September 2020, The Applewood Cycling Group Ride is surely one of the longest continually running weekly group rides on Zwift. Join leader Stephen Collins for a challenging B+ tempo training ride in the lavender fields of France covering two full laps of the Douce route. Our ride incorporates both a steady group with the leader targeting pulls on the front at 3.5 to 3.9 WKG (drafting average ~3.2wkg), and we offer an all-out A+ pace breakaway group. Our breakaway is fully sanctioned and an important element of our group ride dynamic. Every now and then the beacon group catches the break, but only very rarely. No fence, proud. No sweep. We do honor the finish line with a competitive sprint!

We encourage friendly group banter during the ride. Our goal is to create an outstanding training ride that is social and entertaining. Thanks to all our wonderful regulars and a big welcome to all newcomers.

description:

We encourage that all participants head over to zwiftpower.com and register. For more information see: https://zwiftinsider.com/zwiftpower-signup/ Riders who have not completed the Zwiftpower registration will not be included in the official race results. We also ask that your Zwift activities be saved publicly, and that you open and maintain a Strava account to allow for organizer analysis. Any rider exhibiting questionable performance during a the race may be disqualified.

RULES:
- No zPower riders.
- Heart rate monitors mandatory for all categories
- 5min and 20min CEVAZ limits apply. Riding in the wrong category will lead to disqualification.

RACE CATEGORIES:
A: 4.0 W/kg to 5.0 W/kg
B: 3.2 W/kg to 3.99 W/kg
C: 2.5 W/kg to 3.19 W/kg
D: Under 2.49 W/kg

name: DBR Base Endurance Ride
description:
Join the Danish Bike Riders for an endurance workout that will boost your aerobic threshold and train your body to use fat as energy rather than quickly depleting your glycogen stores. Continual efforts will boost your race performance and endurance.

This ride will have a ride leader, but the point is that everyone rides at their own level.

Stay in the blue power zone (zone 2) for the duration of the workout. You will quickly form grupettos with people of your own fitness level.

To bring up the power graph, press G on your PC or Mac. Tap the screen and the graph icon for IOS and Android.

E category - But 1.0-5.0 W/kg avg.

Official site : Danish Bike Riders - https://www.facebook.com/DanishBikeRiders

We highly recommend doing one of the FTP tests as the estimated FTP can be inaccurate and make the difficulty level of the workouts too high for your current fitness level.

For more info on FTP go to: https://support.zwift.com/hc/en-us/articles/210208083-What-is-FTP-and-how-is-it-used-in-Zwift

name: WTRL Team Time Trial - Zone 13
description:
WTRL Team Time Trial #391

Our weekly WTRL Team Time Trial (TTT) allows teams of 3-8 Zwifters to race against the clock together throughout the day to achieve the fastest possible times. Teams are arranged into WTRL's unique Coffee Classes and feature both women's only Coffee Classes and mixed gender too.
  
 There are 30 racing events and teams can be registered up 30 minutes before each race event starts at www.wtrl.racing/ttt-home/ and you can pick your start time from the available slots. Each team is issued a unique RacePass that must be clicked by each team member to gain access to the event for sign-up. You'll also be able to check out the rules, course records and results which update live throughout the day.
  
 Teams & Riders must be registered with www.WTRL.racing and you'll need to be sharing data, via your Zwift Profile Connections with www.zwiftpower.com.
  
 If you are looking for a team, head to our dedicated WTRL TTT Facebook page where plenty of teams are always happy to welcome guest riders and new team mates (https://www.facebook.com/groups/WTRLTTT). Not on Facebook? Feel free to drop us an email with your preferred WTRL TTT Zone and current Zwift Category

Get ready to build next-level fitness with our 9-week OutSeason cycling series! Join us every Tuesday and Thursday for a focused, one-hour session designed to boost your strength, endurance, and power. With just two workouts per week, you’ll start building winter strength that will prepare you to reach your goals next season. This program is tried-and-true, with over 10,000 athletes using it to succeed in cycling and triathlon for over 16 years.

Why settle for base miles alone when you can add targeted intensity this winter? Join Endurance Nation and see what a season of smart training can do. Discover more about the OutSeason at www.endurancenation.us/zwift.

Love these workouts? Check out the club for more opportunities to train with us! We offer social rides on Saturdays, Sundays and Mondays each week — they are great alternates to these scheduled workouts!

name: Run in the Park Autumn Run League - Week 2
description:
IMPORTANT: You must be registered with ZwiftPower for your result to be included in the official Run in the Park results at www.runinthepark.co.uk

Run in the Park Autumn Run League 2026

Join us for a 6-week Zwift running league with a different route and distance each week.

Each round awards league points based on your finishing position within your group, with your best 5 results from 6 counting towards the final standings.

Choose your group based on your current 5K average pace:

A – Faster than 4:29 min/km
B – 4:29 to 5:00 min/km
C – 5:00 to 5:46 min/km
D – Slower than 5:46 min/km

Please choose your group honestly. Your group should be based on your normal 5K ability rather than the distance or expected pace of that week's race.  Runners exceeding the group threshold maybe promoted to the faster group in the results.

Autumn League routes:

Week 1 – Makuri Islands – Mech Isle Loop – 4.1 km
Week 2 – New York – Shuman Trail Loop – 2.8 km
Week 3 – Paris – Rues in Rythme – 5.3 km
Week 4 – Watopia – Splash and Dash – 6.2 km
Week 5 – Yorkshire – Queen's Highway – 5.6 km
Week 6 – Scotland – Glasgow Crit Circuit – 3.2 km

The league starts on Thursday 8 October, with events scheduled at 2-hour intervals throughout the day.

After the league is decided, Week 7 is the Queen Stage – a special 10 km mass-start finale.

The Queen Stage does not count towards the league standings. All groups start together for one final race, with overall and group honours up for grabs.

6 scoring rounds. Best 5 count. One 10K Queen Stage finale.

name: NORDIC CHASE – DOUBLE DRAFT
description:
CAN YOU STAY AWAY – OR CAN YOU CATCH THEM?

Nordic Chase is a twice-weekly staggered-start chase race. All five Zwift Racing Score groups race the same route and finish line, but the lower-score groups start first and the faster groups chase from behind. When riders are caught, they may try to jump onto the faster group's wheels and continue in the draft. The intended overall winner is the first rider across the finish line, regardless of category. Category results may also be shown.

name: Film My Run 500 with NoblePro
description:
Join Stephen Cousins and NoblePro for a 500 metre climb. Set your treadmill to 12% incline and run 4.2km of distance to reach 500 metres elevation. If your treadmill doesn't go that high, set it as high as it will go and join us anyway!

The run will be progressive starting at a walking pace of 5kph rising to 7kph for the final kilometre. Get on to the balls of your toes and get your calf muscles to do the work. This continuous uphill effort will help build strength and endurance for those hilly trail runs
